title: The rail's '+N more' / 'fewer' buttons are 22px tall, under the 24px target
body:
## Summary
Rail.module.css `.more` is 12px mono at line-height 1 with 5px vertical padding: a 22px-tall target, below WCAG 2.5.8's 24px minimum, sitting 2px under the last facet row.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/library/Rail.module.css:21 `.more{margin:var(--sp-nudge) 0 0 var(--sp-4);...font:600 var(--fs-micro)/1 var(--mono);padding:var(--sp-tight) var(--sp-2)}` -> 12 + 2*5 = 22px. The spacing exception of 2.5.8 needs a 24px circle clear of neighbours; the FacetRow above is 2px away (--sp-nudge). Fixed: `min-height:var(--sp-7)` (24px) with inline-flex centring, or a role token for a minimum target.

## Flow
- open the Library rail on a phone or tablet
- a group of 10+ values shows '+3 more'
- the button's box measures 22px tall
- fix: min-height 24px on .more

## Expected impact
Touch users hit the fold control reliably; the rail grows 2px per folded group. Could break: nothing structural; a screenshot shows the extra 2px.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the fold control meets the 24px target size
Before: 22px computed from tokens (fs-micro 12px, line-height 1, sp-tight 5px x2)
After: 24px under min-height:var(--sp-7) (arithmetic)
Method: simulation - token arithmetic only; the rendered box needs the live lane, which this round may not run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/ui/src/components/library/Rail.module.css:21 .more{...font:600 var(--fs-micro)/1 var(--mono);...padding:var(--sp-tight) var(--sp-2)...}
packages/ui/tokens/source.json fs-micro 12px, sp-tight 5px, sp-nudge 2px
instrument: tests/live/legibility.live.spec.ts or library.live: boundingBox of #lib-rail button:has-text('more') height >= 24

title: The rail's fold can say '+1 more' or '+2 more' though its rule says never
body:
## Summary
foldValues opens a group only by its value count (<= 9), so a group of 10-11 values with a selected value past row seven draws '+1 more' / '+2 more' - against the rule stated in library.ts's header, INVENTORY.md and the test's own name.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/library/library.ts:9-10 and :93-95 ('+2 more costs a click to save two lines'), INVENTORY.md row Rail ('only when it hides more than two') and the test name 'unless the rest is two or fewer' all state the rule by what is HIDDEN; the code (library.ts:98, `values.length <= FOLD_AT + 2`, the prototype's own condition) states it by what EXISTS, and pulling a selected value forward hides fewer. The test then pins `expect(f.hidden).toBe(2)` - an assertion that contradicts its own title. Either the code applies the rule after the selection (open when values.length - shown.length <= 2), or the three sentences say 'by value count'. The mutant `library-fold-hides-two` in tests/mutants-unit/registry.ts finds that exact line, so a code change must update that entry in the same commit.

## Flow
- a facet group with 10 values, the 10th pressed
- foldValues(values,false): shown 8, hidden 2
- the rail draws '+2 more'
- fix A: after the filter, return all when hidden <= 2 (and update the mutant's find); fix B: correct the three sentences

## Expected impact
A pressed filter near the fold no longer leaves a '+1 more' button to save one line. Could break: the mutant registry entry goes stale if the line moves.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the fold obeys one stated rule
Before: foldValues(10 values, #10 selected) hidden=2 -> '+2 more' (library.test pins it)
After: hidden=0, no fold button (predicted)
Method: simulation - the case is measured but the fix moves a pinned test and a mutant anchor outside scope (tests/mutants-unit), and the prototype parity question is the owner's
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: library.test fold case flipped to hidden 0 for 10 values with #10 selected, plus the mutant registry entry re-anchored and re-run (npm run test:mutants or its equivalent)

title: Every held tile re-renders on each selection step
body:
## Summary
LibraryTile and LibraryRow are plain function components; the results window re-creates every held option on each arrow key, so a step re-renders ~60-120 tiles to change two.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/library/LibraryTile.tsx:60 and LibraryRow.tsx:28 are not memoized and take fresh onSelect/onOpen closures from the caller (app/(studio)/library/_library/Results.tsx, outside this context). Library.tsx's header promises arrows at key-repeat speed; each step pays for the whole window. Fixed: memo the two options with a stable (id) => void handler pair from Results.

## Flow
- hold the down arrow in a 4-column grid
- selection changes -> Results re-renders every held option
- fix: React.memo on LibraryTile/LibraryRow, onSelect(id)/onOpen(id) passed once

## Expected impact
Fewer renders per key step on large windows; measured by React Profiler commit count. Could break: a stale closure if the handler shape is changed partially.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one selection step re-renders 2 options, not the window
Before: every held option per step (by reading: no memo, closures per render)
After: 2 per step (predicted)
Method: simulation - no DOM profiler in the unit lane; the seam is in Results.tsx, outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/ui/src/components/library/LibraryTile.tsx:60 export function LibraryTile({ card, selected, domId, onSelect, onOpen }: LibraryTileProps)
packages/ui/src/components/library/LibraryRow.tsx:28 export function LibraryRow(...)
instrument: live spec counting React Profiler onRender commits for [role=option] across 10 ArrowDown presses, before/after

title: A locked style shows its lock in the grid but not in the list
body:
## Summary
LibraryTile draws a lock for card.locked; LibraryRow draws nothing for it, so switching to the list loses the one mark that says a style's block can no longer change.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/library/LibraryTile.tsx:83 renders <FloorGlyph name="lock"> when card.locked; LibraryRow.tsx has no reference to `locked` (grep: 0). The accessible name carries 'locked' in both since this round's cardName fix; the visual channel does not. Fixed: the lock glyph beside the row's title, as the attention chip is.

## Flow
- filter to Styles, grid view: ratified styles wear a lock
- switch to list view
- no lock on the same rows
- fix: FloorGlyph lock in the row's .name span

## Expected impact
Grid and list say the same thing about an item. Could break: the name column narrows by one glyph.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the grid and the list show the same marks
Before: lock drawn in 1 of 2 views (grep locked: LibraryTile 1, LibraryRow 0)
After: 2 of 2
Method: probe - the grep is the figure; the rendered result needs cx-capture, the director's
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: cx-capture library list view of Styles before/after, plus a library.test render asserting the row markup carries the lock svg when card.locked
